title: Datetime 'seconds'/'milliseconds' temporal serialization must apply the tz offset (use timestamp_tz)
answers: datetime with timezone serialized to wrong unix timestamp with ser_json_temporal='seconds'
temporal_mode milliseconds ignores tzinfo / UTC offset
to_json of aware datetime does not match datetime.timestamp()
dict keys of datetimes serialized as epoch numbers are off by the timezone offset
body:
Symptom: with config `ser_json_temporal`/`temporal_mode` set to 'seconds' or 'milliseconds', a tz-aware datetime (e.g. UTC-5) serialized to an epoch number that ignored its offset, so it didn't match Python's `dt.timestamp()`. Both values and dict keys were affected (JSON mode).
Root cause: `pydantic-core/src/serializers/type_serializers/datetime_etc.rs:datetime_to_seconds` / `datetime_to_milliseconds` added up `dt.date.timestamp()` and the time-of-day seconds, so `dt.time.tz_offset` was never used.
Fix pattern: build the epoch from speedate's `DateTime::timestamp_tz()`, which subtracts the offset, then add the fractional part from `dt.time.microsecond` (divide by 1e6 for seconds, 1e3 for ms; multiply the whole seconds by 1000 for ms).
Constraints: this applies only to full datetimes. `date_to_seconds` and the time helpers have no offset to apply. If you add another numeric temporal mode, compute it from `timestamp_tz()`, not from the date and time parts separately. Tests go in `pydantic-core/tests/serializers/test_datetime.py` (`test_config_datetime_tz_aware`). They check `to_python(mode='json')`, `to_json`, and the dict-key form against `dt.timestamp()`.
applies: pydantic-core datetime serialization with ser_json_temporal seconds/milliseconds
